subject: Intermittent upload failures to on-prem tenant -> packets dropped mid-stream
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma@clearday.co>
To: support@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent uploads to our on-prem instance failing mid-stream

Hi Redwood team,

We're seeing repeated failures when large file uploads (>=50MB) from our app hit our on-prem tenant behind the private connector. Uploads start but stall and eventually time out after ~60s. Small files are fine. This started yesterday after a routine network maintenance window on our side.

What we've observed: 
- Traceroute shows an MTU-discovery ICMP reply partway through (attached).
- Some TCP sessions show RST after a burst of retransmits.
- We captured a short tcpdump showing fragmented packets and retransmits (attached pcap).

Can you confirm whether any SNAT / conntrack limits or MTU clamping on the Redwood edge could cause mid-stream drops? Our NetOps suspect path MTU or asymmetric routing causing broken DF handling.

Attaching: clearpath_traceroute_20261110.txt, tcpdump_fragment_sample_20261110.pcap

Thanks,
Emma Liu
Senior SRE, ClearDay Inc.
emma@clearday.co
+1 415 555 0112
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma@clearday.co>, netops@clearday.co
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent uploads to our on-prem instance failing mid-stream

Thanks Emma — sorry you're hitting this. I pulled the attachments and started an initial triage. High level summary and immediate asks below.

Initial observations:
- The traceroute shows an ICMP "fragmentation needed" at hop 5. That suggests a PMTU issue on the path (DF bit set + MTU lower than probe).
- The pcap contains fragmented IPv4 fragments followed by multiple retransmits and then a RST from the server side.

Immediate asks from our side (so we can rule things out quickly):
1) Can your NetOps provide the MTU on the edge interface facing the Redwood connection and confirm if they are clamping MSS for TCP (we often see middleboxes that don't handle DF correctly).
2) If possible, run `conntrack -S` and `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_conntrack_max` on the on-prem gateway and share the output — we want to check for conntrack resource exhaustion.
3) Please share the complete tcpdump for a full session if available (we only have a 12s snippet).

On our side I'll: 
- Escalate to infra network on the Redwood edge (cc'ing Monica for connection-side snapshots).
- Provision a capture at the regional handoff and check SNAT ephemeral port utilization for your tenant during the window you observed.

I'll follow up with a targeted rollback plan if we find a configuration change on our edge.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Staff Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Liu <emma@clearday.co>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent uploads to our on-prem instance failing mid-stream

Vivek / team — quick update from the edge snapshots I ran overnight and the tenant-level metrics: 

What I collected:
- Attachment: redwood_conntrack_snapshot_20261111.txt (conntrack counters and SNAT table dump for tenant ID CLRD-001)
- Per-route MTU on egress interface: 1500 (no unusual lowering).
- SNAT ephemeral port usage peaked at ~88% of the allocated pool at 09:05 PST while we see multiple sockets in TIME_WAIT.

Interpretation & likely cause:
- Conntrack pressure + lots of TIME_WAIT on short-lived upload control sockets looks like conntrack table exhaustion is causing new sessions to be dropped; when that happens we often observe connection resets and retransmit storms.
- The pcap shows fragments — but fragmentation alone wouldn't explain the periodicity unless some devices are dropping fragments under load. Possible combined failure: mid-path PMTU discovery + conntrack saturation.

Suggested immediate mitigations (short term):
1) Increase SNAT ephemeral port pool for CLRD-001 and bump conntrack max on the edge for the tenant by +30% (we can do scoped, non-tenant-global change).
2) Ask ClearDay to enable MSS clamping on their gateway to 1400 as a temporary workaround to avoid fragmentation while we validate path MTU.
3) Schedule a 15-min test window tomorrow 09:00-09:15 PST where we will monitor per-flow telemetry and run a full end-to-end capture.

I can push the SNAT/conntrack increase if Vivek approves — it will be a quick config change with a one-minute control-plane rotation.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Edge Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Emma Liu <emma@clearday.co>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent uploads to our on-prem instance failing mid-stream

Thanks Monica — that aligns with my read. Approved: do the scoped SNAT/conntrack increase for CLRD-001 now (non-global).

Planned actions (executed):
- Monica: applied +30% conntrack and +20% ephemeral port allocation to CLRD-001 at 16:20 PST. Change window was non-disruptive.
- Marissa: scheduling the test window with ClearDay for Friday 09:00 PST and will share the dial-in & runbook.
- Karthik: please validate there are no security group rules we accidentally loosened in the tenant mapping that could let in unexpected traffic; we want just the port/conntrack knobs changed.

Next steps for the customer: Emma, please run the same file upload during the Friday window and provide a full tcpdump so we can confirm the failure mode: if uploads succeed consistently after the change and MSS clamp, we'll still pursue a long-term fix: trace down the middlebox that drops fragments and work with ClearDay's carrier to adjust PMTU handling.

I'll keep the incident open and report after the Friday test.

-Vivek
